Application Materials.content:
- **Application essay:** An application essay is a key component of the application process and must accompany the initial application. The statement should capture your motivation to pursue the MSc in People Analytics and Human-Centric Management at University College London in a genuine and specific manner; demonstrate a clear interest in people management, organisational behaviour, social psychology, data analytics, and statistics, as well as prior experience and knowledge in these areas; specify your career aspirations after completing the degree, outlining well-researched and grounded short- and long-term professional and personal objectives; and cover why you are looking to pursue this programme, what you will bring to the UCL communities, and evidence of leadership and teamwork.
- **CV:** “We also require a copy of your CV.”
- **Required documents:** “You will need to include a degree transcript in one of the suggested disciplines, two references, and a personal statement.”
- **English evidence:** Applicants are encouraged to include evidence of their English language qualification at the time they apply. Overseas applicants should also supply evidence of their English language ability through one of UCL’s accepted [English Language Tests.](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/english-language-requirements)
- **Current students:** If your predicted final results meet the minimum entry requirements, you can apply before receiving final degree results; include details of predicted results on the application form and an official transcript of results so far.
- **References:** References should be provided digitally by your referee unless this is not possible due to accessibility requirements, in which case contact the [UCL referees team](mailto:eferees.pgadmissions@ucl.ac.uk).

Interview Requirements.content: Applicants who meet the entry requirements and provide an appropriate professional statement will be reviewed. Those considered eligible for the next stage will be invited to an online video interview, with the invitation sent by email from Kira Talent. Interview performance is a crucial component of the application process, as it provides evidence of the applicant’s genuine interest in the programme and the specific qualities sought: excellence, drive, critical thinking, integrity, and teamwork skills.

Application Deadlines.content:
**Start date:** September 2026
**Application deadline:** Applications for the 2026/27 cycle will open on **20th October 2025** and close on **26th June 2026 at 5pm UK time for applicants who require a visa**; and on **28th August 2026** for those who do not.
A staged admissions process is in place for this programme.

Academic Requirements.content:
- A minimum of an **upper second-class Bachelor's degree from a UK university or an overseas qualification of an equivalent standard**, in relevant subjects, such as **business and management, social psychology, and social sciences**.
- Degrees and work experience in other fields are also considered if students have a strong motivation to pursue a career in people and management-related areas.
- Applicants are expected to have a **basic understanding of statistics, business, and management** through formal or informal education and work experience, and should be prepared for quantitative, managerial, and people management topics.
- China-specific equivalency: A **four-year bachelor's degree from a recognised Chinese higher education institution** will be considered; the required grade varies depending on the awarding university.
- China-specific equivalency for the required upper second-class (2:1): applicants from UCL's list of Chinese universities, which includes a selection of **Project 211, Project 985, and Double First-Class universities**, need a Bachelor's degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 85%**.
- China-specific equivalency for the required upper second-class (2:1): applicants from all other universities recognised by the Chinese Ministry of Education need a Bachelor's degree with a **minimum weighted average mark of 90%**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- The English language level for this course is: **Level 2**. Further information can be found on UCL's [English language requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/learning-and-living-ucl/international-students/english-language-requirements) page.
- [UCL Pre-Master's and Pre-sessional English courses](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/languages-international-education/preparation-courses) are for international students who are aiming to study for a postgraduate degree at UCL.
- IELTS Academic: **Level 2: Overall score of 7.0 and a minimum of 6.5 in each component**. IELTS Academic Online is accepted; IELTS One Skill Retake is not accepted.
- TOEFL: UCL will continue to accept the TOEFL iBT after 21 January 2026. Tests taken from 21 January 2026: **Level 2: Overall score of 4.5 and 4.5 in reading, writing, speaking and listening**. Tests taken before 21 January 2026: **Level 2: Overall score of 96 with 24/30 in reading and writing and 22/30 in speaking and listening**. TOEFL iBT Special Home Edition is accepted; TOEFL iBT MyBestScore is not acceptable. UCL’s institution code for TOEFL is **9163**.
- Cambridge English: C2 Proficiency (CPE): **Level 2: Overall score of 180 with 172 in all subtests**.
- Cambridge English: C1 Advanced (CAE): **Level 2: Overall score of 180 with 172 in all subtests**.
- Pearson Test of English (Academic): **Level 2: Overall score of 76 with a minimum of 75 in each Communicative Skill**.

Program Overview.content:
The UCL People Analytics and Human-Centric Management MSc is a full-time, one-calendar-year programme in London, Canary Wharf. Developed in partnership with industry leaders, it is designed to give students critical and latest knowledge and skills in people analytics, leadership, and the future of work, and is aimed at those aspiring to careers in management, people analytics, and human resources.
Organisations today face complex challenges related to people management and leadership, such as attracting and retaining top talent, ensuring employee engagement and well-being, and adapting to rapid technological changes. The programme combines fundamental HR and management knowledge with cutting-edge research and practice in people analytics, strategic management, work design, and employee well-being. Its curriculum goes beyond traditional HR education so students can gain the skills required to lead sustainable change and growth in various organisations, focusing on people not just as resources but as individuals with needs, values, and potential.
The programme is ideal for students aiming for high-level careers in people analytics, HR analytics, management, or HR. It covers quantitative, managerial, and people management topics and welcomes applicants from a wide variety of academic backgrounds, including business and management, social psychology, and social sciences.
This degree offers opportunities to:
- Acquire the skills and knowledge required to lead organisations, not only to drive business success, but also promote a healthier society and work environment.
- Develop analytical skills to inform strategic decisions and navigate organisational issues through a people- and human-centric approach.
- Benefit from a bespoke Careers and Employer Engagement Programme and a dedicated careers team.
- Learn from expert faculty producing research rated as ‘world-leading’ and ‘internationally excellent’ in the latest [Research Excellence Framework (REF 2021)](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/news/95-som-research-outputs-world-leading-internationally-excellent-ref). The teaching team is comprised of academic leads and practitioners, exposing students to cutting-edge research and industry knowledge.
- Study on levels 38 and 50 of Canary Wharf’s One Canada Square in state-of-the-art lecture theatres, with purpose-built student facilities, hubs, and quiet study spaces.
As graduates, students are equipped with essential HR and analytics knowledge, a multifaceted skillset, and attributes for strategic, people-focused roles across multiple industries. Developed in collaboration with employers and guided by an advisory board of industry leaders and experts in people and management, the programme prepares graduates for roles including People Analytics Consultant, Workforce Strategy Analyst, Employee Experience Designer, Organisational Development Specialist, HR Technology Analyst, Leadership Development Advisor, Diversity & Inclusion Manager, and Change Management Consultant.
The programme offers networking opportunities through careers workshops with employers, alumni events with other postgraduate students from the UCL School of Management, access to UCL societies and clubs, engagement with the global business community in Canary Wharf, one-on-one careers advice, exclusive corporate events, the alumni community, and the School of Management’s [New Technologies & Innovation Speaker Series](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/newtechnologyspeakerseries) and [Business Leader Speaker Series](https://www.mgmt.ucl.ac.uk/business-leaders-speaker-series).
UCL School of Management is AACSB accredited, a global mark of excellence recognising its commitment to innovative, research-led teaching, rigorous academic standards, and preparing students for impactful global careers in business and management.
The programme is delivered through lectures, case studies, class discussions and group projects. Students typically study compulsory modules in Terms 1 and 2, while the Dissertation project takes place over Term 3. The programme also includes multiple bootcamps throughout the year, where industry leaders teach the latest knowledge and techniques in data analytics, artificial intelligence, and organisational design. Assessment is through written examinations, individual/group coursework, and a 12,000-word dissertation project, which typically involves practical topics chosen by the student and addresses people-related challenges faced by organisations. Students undertake modules to the value of 180 credits; upon successful completion of 180 credits, they are awarded an MSc in People Analytics and Human-Centric Management.

Curriculum.content:
Study mode: **Full-time**. Duration: **1 calendar year**. Location: London, Canary Wharf.
The programme is delivered through a combination of lectures, case studies, class discussions and group projects. Students typically study **4 compulsory modules, each worth 15 credits in Terms 1 and 2**. The Dissertation project takes place over Term 3. In addition to the core modules, the programme includes multiple bootcamps throughout the year, where industry leaders visit to teach the latest knowledge and techniques in data analytics, artificial intelligence, and organisational design.
Assessment is through written examinations, individual/group coursework, and a **12,000-word dissertation project**. The dissertation project will typically involve practical topics chosen by the student, and address a range of people-related challenges faced by organisations.
Each taught module in Terms 1 and 2 is delivered over 10 weeks, with 3 contact hours per week comprising lecture content and interactive components. Students can expect approximately 12 contact hours per week in Terms 1 and 2, plus approximately 7-12 hours a week for each module on assessment and independent study. The total number of weekly hours will vary from 20 - 25 hours according to the module and activities. Contact hours reduce to approximately 2-5 hours per week during Term 3, when students focus on their dissertation module.
Full-time compulsory modules:
- [Data Visualisation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/data-visualisation-MSIN0167)
- [Leadership and Communication](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/leadership-and-communication-MSIN0077)
- [Organisational Behaviour B](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/organisational-behaviour-b-MSIN0142)
- [Influence and Negotiations](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/influence-and-negotiations-MSIN0148)
- [Managing Diversity](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/managing-diversity-MSIN0236)
- [Strategic Human Resources Management](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/strategic-human-resources-management-MSIN0265)
- [People Analytics](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/people-analytics-MSIN0266)
- [Sustainable Work Design](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/sustainable-work-design-MSIN0267)
- [Dissertation](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/module-catalogue/modules/dissertation-MSIN0268)
The compulsory modules provide the basis and foundation in key HR theories and Data Analytics knowledge and bootcamps give students the opportunity to gain in-depth knowledge about more specialised areas of HR management. The compulsory dissertation module (research project) takes place in Term 3. Throughout the year the programme will expose students to opportunities to identify dissertation topics, such as inequity in organisations, adoption of flexible work policies, and leading remote teams.
Students undertake modules to the value of **180 credits**. Upon successful completion of **180 credits**, students will be awarded an MSc in People Analytics and Human-Centric Management.

Financial Aid.content:
- **MSc People Analytics and Human-Centric Management Scholarships:** A total of **£20,000** of scholarships are available for outstanding candidates on the programme. All applicants who apply to study MSc People Analytics and Human-Centric Management at UCL and who meet the scholarship criteria will be considered for scholarship funding.
- UCL offers a range of scholarships across all programmes. Postgraduate scholarships are typically awarded to the most talented students across a range of categories, and applicants wishing to obtain scholarships are strongly encouraged to apply early.
- **UCL Global Master’s Scholarship:** Enables and encourages international students from lower income backgrounds to pursue full-time Master’s degree studies at UCL. There are **85 scholarships available each year worth up to £15,000 each**, awarded on the basis of financial need and upon the recommendation of the Student Funding Office. [Learn more about the UCL Global Master’s Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/ucl-global-masters-scholarship)
- **UCL Musubi Global Master’s Scholarship (Japan):** One scholarship of **£20,250** is available to a Japanese student applying to study during the **2026/2027** academic year. [Learn more about the Musubi Global Master’s Scholarship](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/musubi-global-masters-scholarship)
- **UCL Fee Partnerships:** UCL has partnerships with external funding providers in which the university offers a contribution towards tuition fees. Applicants selected for relevant external awards, who are also offered a place at UCL, automatically qualify for the fee contribution. [View the complete list of fee partnerships](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/fee-partnerships)
- **Fullbright Commission Award:** Available for a US graduate student or those with equivalent experience in a relevant field to study any MSc programme at the UCL School of Management. This is only available to citizens of the United States of America. [Learn more about the Fullbright Commission Award](https://fulbright.org.uk/our-programmes/fulbright-scholarships-to-the-uk/us-postgraduates/)
- UCL recommends using [UCL’s Scholarship Finder](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships/scholarships-finder) to find all scholarships available. [Learn more about scholarships at UCL](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/scholarships)

Multiple Applications.content: Please note - you can only apply to a **maximum of two taught graduate courses in any academic cycle**.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
UCL does not accept requests to defer. However, UCL will consider a request to defer only in the following circumstances:
- The serious illness of the offer holder or the serious illness of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The death of a parent, guardian, partner or child of the offer holder.
- The need to take parental or adoption leave during the next 12 months.
- Where the offer holder is directly and severely affected by a natural or human-made disaster (i.e., war, earthquakes or flooding).
- The offer holder has been awarded a UCL scholarship (including UCL partnership agreements and Faculty awards); or a full scholarship (tuition fee and maintenance support) from a recognised funding body - for study in the following academic year. (A ‘scholarship’ does not include student loans. The UCL Student Funding office can confirm the standing of a funding body or partnership as required).
- The offer holder holds an offer to study the UCL International Pre-Masters.
To be eligible for a deferral you must hold an unconditional offer which you have accepted. The exception is if you hold an offer for the International Pre-Masters, in which case an accepted conditional offer is allowed. You must also have paid the tuition fee deposit in full or be marked as exempt (if a deposit requirement is in place for your programme). If you wish to defer but do not fall into one of the above categories you are most welcome to apply for the next academic year once applications open, however, applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that intake.
If you need to request a deferral for one of the above reasons you will need to do so on the offer page of your application portal. If requesting a deferral due to illness or parental or adoption leave you will need to provide a letter from a relevant medical practitioner. If your request is made on the basis that you have been awarded a scholarship for study in the following academic year you will be required to upload a copy of your official scholarship award letter. UCL reserves the right to request more information from the offer holder, scholarship body or medical practitioner before making a final decision.
An application cannot be deferred twice. Applicants wanting to defer for two years must re-apply and be considered as a new application in competition with other applicants.
The deadline for requesting a deferral is **two weeks prior to the start of the course**.
If your deferral request is unsuccessful and you cannot join this year, you are most welcome to apply for the next academic year once applications open, however, applications will be considered anew and in competition with all other applications for that particular intake.
If you have had your deferral request approved, you will receive a new offer letter. You may need to take a new English test if your current English language qualification expires before the revised start date.
If your request to defer is approved, any tuition fee deposit payments will be held on account until enrolment.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- If you are currently studying and do not yet have final results, and your predicted final results meet the minimum entry requirements, you can apply before receiving your final degree results. You should include details of your predicted results and an official transcript of your results so far; if an offer is made, **it will be conditional** and you will need to prove that you meet the condition **before the beginning of the programme**.
- You may apply without a current English test as long as you send your qualification as soon as you receive it. If offered a place, **it will be conditional** on providing evidence of meeting UCL’s [English Language Requirements](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/prospective-students/graduate/english-language-requirements) **before the start of the programme**.
